text:
ash: FYI saw a small p95 bump in tonight's canary for cohorts with long-lived sessions. pattern looks like KV cold misses + cross-region latency when a host drains.
ash: impact: ~3% of requests had ~2x p95 for ~10m. not catastrophic but noisy for users.
priya: was affinity preserved?
ash: yes, sticky sessions + cross-region replica placement. when we move traffic the local prefix isn't always warm and some targets fetch from remote region.
ben: interesting corner: we have tenant A with very high prefix reuse causing heavy prefetch ops; tenant B has low reuse. we need per-tenant strategy.
anya: idea: "lease-grace tokens". when initiating a drain, issue N grace-tokens per active session that permit the source host to serve/forward without immediate eviction for X seconds while async prefetch is happening. tokens are conservatively consumed for long-sessions only.
priya: how is this different from sticky-hold? token makes it explicit and measurable and lets us account for SLO credits. also allows per-tenant policies (VIPs get more tokens).
ash: exactly. tokens plus a tenant-priority lane: prefetch workers prioritize VIP tokens; non-VIP gets best-effort. combine with cross-region warm-proxies that accept prefetch RPCs and keep small transient caches to absorb remote fetches.
ben: we should also add an "slo-credit" ledger: if a cohort incurs extra p95 while warming, we deduct credits from the rollout budget; if credits exhausted -> automatic fallback. this prevents silent degradation.
priya: compact decision signals: token_exhaustion, prefetch_hit_rate, target_p95_ratio, cross_region_miss_rate. routing plane makes local decisions per-cohort; central controller monitors aggregated credits.
anya: proposal config (stored as strings in proto):
```json
{"strategy":"lease-grace","grace_tokens":"2","token_ttl_s":"120","prefetch_priority":"tenant_priority","slo_credit_budget":"1000","p95_ratio_fallback":"1.5","cross_region_miss_thresh":"0.1"}
```
ben: ops UX: Console should show token usage per-cohort, slo_credit_remaining, prefetch_hit_rate, and a simple colored handoff-state (prefetching/probing/committed/fallback). make it very scannable.
priya: alerts: page if slo_credit_remaining < 10% OR cross_region_miss_rate > threshold for >5m. rollout-bot: will emit token-usage and credit events to the rollout stream.
ash: implementation notes: 1) router issue grace-token at drain start and decrement on successful handoff or TTL expiry, 2) prefetch worker honors tenant_priority, uses a short-lived region-local cache, 3) a central ledger service tracks slo credits per rollout cohort and can trigger central stop.
ben: testing plan: unit tests for token lifecycle and credit accounting; sim with mixed-tenant workloads to tune defaults; canary running with token TTLs and banked credits; chaos test injecting cross-region latency.
anya: runbook: on fallback event check token usage, prefetch_hit_rate, which tenants drained, cross-region misses. Actions: 1) pause rollout, 2) top-up tokens for VIPs from global pool, 3) increase prefetch_priority for affected tenants, 4) if unresolved rollback.
priya: question: do grace-tokens add risk of prolonging bad hosts? TTL small (120s) and tokens limited to active sessions only; also we monitor target_p95 and will revoke tokens if target_p95 spikes.
ash: good point. revoke path: router can mark token-revoked for cohort if probe_failures > 0.2 or p95_ratio > threshold.
ben: cost tradeoff: prefetch and warm-proxy caches add ops and memory, but we expect less user-visible rollback and fewer rollbacks overall. sim will estimate ops cost vs rollback cost savings.
anya: I'll add Console panels and a simple UI control to top-up VIP tokens manually. priya: i'll draft the RFC and include token lifecycle, ledger proto, and runbook.
rollout-bot: scheduled-canary: job 2026-06-01T02:00Z created for variant v14; will report token/credit events to eng-platform.
priya: thx all. if no objections i'll open RFC today and loop in eng-oncall for the first 72h after rollout. :thumbsup:
